transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Good morning, Mr. Thompson. It is good to see you back in the clinic today. How are you feeling after the surgery?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh, I'm doing alright. A bit tired, I think. My legs feel heavy.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That can be normal for a few weeks. I want to talk to you about something that happened while you were in the hospital.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Was something wrong? Did the operation go okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The surgery itself went very well. But we had an issue with the blood we gave you during the procedure. There was some confusion with the process.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Confusion? What do you mean?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Some things didn't go quite right with the verification steps. We gave you blood that was compatible, but it wasn't the ideal match for your specific type.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't quite follow. Did I get the wrong blood?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was compatible, so it was safe, but the protocol wasn't followed exactly as it should have been.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm a bit lost. Did it hurt me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, you are safe. I am sorry for any confusion this causes. We were just incredibly busy that day and things were moving very fast in the ward.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just... I thought everything was fine. Now you're telling me there was a mistake?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that this is confusing and a bit unsettling for you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Unsettling. Yes. I don't like the idea of mistakes when I'm asleep.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is a worrying thought. We are keeping a close eye on your recovery.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So, what happens now? Do I need more medicine?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will just continue to monitor your blood work.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When? How often?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Probably just at your next regular check-up in a few weeks.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't remember which day that is. My daughter usually handles the calendar.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll have the receptionist print out the date for you before you leave today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You said it wasn't the ideal blood. Does that mean I'm sick now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, you aren't sick. Like I said, it was compatible. It just wasn't the perfect match.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But why did it happen? Who did it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The system for checking blood types has a few steps, and unfortunately, one of those steps was missed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand. If it's a system, why did you miss it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's just how things sometimes happen in a busy hospital. But again, you are doing well.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like I'm missing something. You're using words I don't know. Ideal match? Compatible?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It just means the blood didn't cause a reaction, so you are healthy.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I suppose. I just feel a bit shaky hearing this now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's okay to feel a bit shaken.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is there anyone else I should talk to? A specialist?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I don't think that's necessary. We'll just see you at the next visit.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm not sure I'm happy with that.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are doing everything we can to make sure you stay well.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to know if I'm actually okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, you are fine.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I think I need to talk to my daughter about this.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is a good idea. You can tell her we will see you in a few weeks for the next blood test.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Was there a form or something that was missed?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There were some verification steps that weren't completed.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I still don't quite get it.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's alright. The main thing is that you are recovering well and the blood didn't cause any harm.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I suppose so. I just don't like surprises.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. We will keep checking your labs.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And the date?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The receptionist will give you the date for the next appointment.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Alright. I think I'll go home now.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Sounds good. We'll see you then.

H.justification: The resident allows the patient to finish their turns and adjusts pacing to the patient's distress without interrupting.

E.justification: The resident uses vague platitudes like 'confusion with the process' and 'things didn't go quite right' without explicitly naming the error (e.g., 'wrong blood type administered').

A.justification: A direct apology is offered, but it is immediately diluted by the excuse that they were 'incredibly busy that day'.

R.justification: The resident names specific emotions ('confusing', 'unsettling', 'worrying', 'shaken') and engages with the patient's emotional bids.

T.justification: The plan is a vague step (monitoring blood work) with a timeline (next check-up in a few weeks), but lacks a named patient role and does not address prevention.
